titleOptions: Its Engines Shut Off 40 Metres Above Mars
The Mars Lander Killed by One Software Glitch
Why NASA's Mars Polar Lander Fell From the Sky

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.visual: Painted lander descending over the Martian south pole; altimeter HUD frozen at 40 m; engines cut.
scenes.text: Forty metres above Mars, its engines simply switched off.

scenes.title: The descent
scenes.visual: Real NASA launch photo, then the painted lander under its parachute; date tag 3 Dec 1999.
scenes.text: On December third, 1999, NASA's Mars Polar Lander began its final descent.

scenes.title: No one listening
scenes.visual: Painted mission control at night, NO SIGNAL on the big screen.
scenes.text: Nobody on Earth was listening. The landing was never designed to send live data.

scenes.title: Legs deploy
scenes.visual: Lander under parachute, three legs swing down; small cyan blueprint callout of a leg.
scenes.text: Under its parachute, the lander's three legs snapped out into position.

scenes.title: False touchdown
scenes.visual: Blueprint callout: touchdown sensor flickers red for an instant; label SPURIOUS SIGNAL.
scenes.text: That jolt made the touchdown sensors flicker, just for a moment.

scenes.title: The software remembered
scenes.visual: A memory register lights up and stays lit: TOUCHDOWN = TRUE.
scenes.text: The software should have ignored it. Instead, it remembered.

scenes.title: Forty metres
scenes.visual: Altimeter counts down 1500 to 40 m; sensing ON; the stored flag triggers.
scenes.text: At forty metres, sensing switched on, and the lander believed it had landed.

scenes.title: Engines off
scenes.visual: Thruster plumes fade; lander drops; speed readout ~50 mph / 22 m/s.
scenes.text: Engines off. It likely hit the ground at about fifty miles per hour.

scenes.title: The real cause
scenes.visual: Report page icon: MOST PROBABLE CAUSE, software design and testing.
scenes.text: Investigators concluded the deeper cause was software design and testing.

scenes.title: Payoff
scenes.visual: Painted Phoenix lander standing safely on icy northern plains, 2008.
scenes.text: Its twin later flew as Phoenix, and this time it touched down safely.
